content.overview: Any creditor aggrieved by any decision of the Official Liquidator under section 363 may appeal to the Tribunal within thirty days from the date of such decision. The Tribunal may confirm, reverse or modify the decision of the Official Liquidator and make such order as it thinks fit.
content.glance: Creditor aggrieved by Official Liquidator’s decision under s. 363 may appeal to Tribunal within 30 days; Tribunal may confirm, reverse or modify.
content.study: Section 364 provides the appellate route from claim decisions of the Official Liquidator. Any creditor aggrieved by a decision under section 363 may appeal to the Tribunal within thirty days of that decision. The Tribunal may confirm, reverse or modify the decision and make such order as it thinks fit.

sections.heading: Appeal
sections.body: Within 30 days of Official Liquidator’s decision under s. 363; Tribunal may confirm, reverse or modify.

examples.title: Successful appeal
examples.body: A creditor’s claim is reduced by the Official Liquidator. On appeal under s. 364 the Tribunal restores the full amount.

hypotheticals.question: Is the appeal period of 30 days extendable under s. 364?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 364 states an appeal within thirty days; any extension would depend on general Tribunal procedure or limitation principles applicable to such appeals.

misconceptions.trap: There is no appeal from the Official Liquidator’s claim decision.
misconceptions.correction: Section 364 expressly provides an appeal to the Tribunal within thirty days.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 364 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the rule of s. 364. II. Apply to facts. III. Conclude.

examTips: Name s. 364 and its core requirement.
